topic: invert pg DATE parsing with process-local parts, never a fixed timezone
lesson: node-postgres parses a DATE column into a JS Date at LOCAL midnight of the process timezone, so the exact inverse is to read back the PROCESS-LOCAL date parts (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate). Formatting with a hardcoded timeZone such as Asia/Kolkata only happens to work on hosts at or west of that offset and silently returns the previous day on hosts east of it (e.g. Asia/Tokyo), so a date-only normalizer must never pin a timezone.
